app.port_busy_text:
Port {port} is used by another program, so WinAirdrop can't receive files.

Change WINAIRDROP_PORT in WinAirdrop's settings file (.env) or close the other program, then open WinAirdrop again.
app.pick_folder: Where should WinAirdrop save the files you send?

page.title: WinAirdrop Settings
page.subtitle: Receive photos and files from your iPhone on this PC
page.how_1:
Prepare this PC
Two quick checks so your iPhone can reach it.
page.how_2:
Create the Shortcut
Once, on your iPhone. About 3 minutes.
page.how_3:
Share anything
Share → WinAirdrop, and it pops up here.
page.s1_intro: Your iPhone sends files to this PC over your network. These two checks make sure Windows lets them in, and only on networks you trust.
page.ready_all: All set: your iPhone can reach this PC.
page.ready_missing: One step left: fix the item marked in yellow below.
page.fw_desc: The firewall blocks connections coming from other devices. WinAirdrop needs permission to receive them, only on private networks. You only need to do this once.
page.fw_missing: Not allowed yet: your iPhone can't reach this PC.
page.net_desc: Windows labels every network as Private (your home, your own phone hotspot) or Public (cafés, hotels, campus). WinAirdrop only works on Private networks, so nobody on a public network can send files to your PC.
page.net_noprivate: You're only on public networks. If one of them is yours, trust it.
page.net_trust_confirm:
Trust "{name}"?

Only do this for your own network (home Wi-Fi or your iPhone hotspot), never for public Wi-Fi.
page.net_hotspot_tip: Using your iPhone's Personal Hotspot? The first time you connect, Windows marks it as Public. Click Trust this network next to it.
page.admin_note: These buttons ask for administrator permission (a Windows prompt). Click Yes.
page.s2_intro: The Shortcut on your iPhone needs two things: the address of this PC and the token, a password only your PC and your iPhone know.
page.url_help: The address of this PC on your network.
page.token_help: Keep it secret: anyone with it could send you files. Only shown on this PC.
page.qr_help: Point your iPhone camera at it, tap the text that appears and copy it.
page.step_1: On your iPhone, open the Shortcuts app → tap + (top right) → name it WinAirdrop. This is the name you'll see when you tap Share.
page.step_2: Tap the ⓘ button at the bottom → turn on Show in Share Sheet. Leave the accepted types as Any.
page.step_3: A first block appears: “Receive Any input from Share Sheet”. Leave it as it is.
page.step_4: Search for the action Repeat with Each and add it. It should read “Repeat with each item in Shortcut Input”. This sends every selected file, one by one.
page.step_5: Inside the repeat, add the action Get Contents of URL. In the URL field type the address above by hand (don't put a variable there).
page.step_6:
Tap the › arrow of that action and fill in:
  • Method: POST
  • Headers → Add new header: key Authorization, value Bearer followed by your token (scan the QR: it already includes “Bearer”).
  • Request Body: Form → Add new field → File. Key file, value: tap and pick Repeat Item.
page.step_7: After End Repeat, add Show Notification with the text Sent to PC ✅.
page.step_8: Try it: open a photo → Share → WinAirdrop. The first time, iOS asks to find devices on your local network: tap Allow.
page.steps_icloud: With iCloud sync for Shortcuts turned on, the Shortcut also appears on your iPad.
page.steps_warning: If you see “Couldn't convert Rich Text to URL”, a variable ended up in the URL field. Type the address by hand, and put Repeat Item in the form field instead.
page.s3_intro: Changes apply right away when you click Save.
page.folder_help: Folder where everything you send ends up.
page.on_receive_help: Open them on screen works like AirDrop on a Mac. For your safety only photos, videos, audio, PDFs and text files are opened; anything else (like programs) is just shown in File Explorer, never run.
page.rename_desc: Name photos and videos by the date they were taken
page.rename_help: Instead of <kbd>IMG_5107.jpg</kbd> you get <kbd>Photo 2026-09-19 21.13.20.jpg</kbd>, so they sort by date. Other files keep their name.
page.notif_desc: Show a Windows notification when something arrives
page.startup_desc: Run WinAirdrop in the background when I sign in (recommended)
page.startup_help: If it's off, your iPhone can't send anything until you open WinAirdrop yourself.
page.language_help: Language of this page, the notifications and the file names.
page.advanced_intro: You don't need to change these unless something isn't working.
page.name_help: Your iPhone finds this PC as .local. Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. If you change it, update the address in the Shortcut.
page.port_help: Keep 8770 unless another program uses it. If you change it: restart WinAirdrop, click Allow WinAirdrop again and update the address in the Shortcut.
page.restart_banner: The network name or port changed. Restart WinAirdrop to apply it.
page.restart_failed: WinAirdrop didn't come back. Open it again from the Start menu.
page.browse_wait: Choose a folder in the window that just opened…
page.reset_desc: If you think someone else has your token, create a new one. Then update it in your iPhone Shortcut.
page.reset_confirm: Create a new token? The Shortcut on your iPhone will stop working until you paste the new one.
page.err_folder: WinAirdrop can't save files in this folder. Choose another one.
page.err_name: Use only lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens (not at the start or end).
